events.body:
This is a RydeTAXI metered trip from Orchard Road to Marina Bay Sands, and the GPS records +5.4 km actual against a 3.9 km optimal route [F1], with two off-route segments: 14:10–14:13 adding 1.63 km [F4] and 14:17–14:29 adding 2.83 km [F5]. Under RD-1 each segment is reviewed individually and any segment not exempted by RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 is an unexempt detour; RD-2 then refunds, for RydeTAXI, only the unexempt segments' extra_km at the trip's per-km rate [RD-1][RD-2].

Segment 1 (F4) is exempt. The LTA accident reported at 13:52 on Orchard Road towards Bras Basah was 30 m from the optimal route, so within the matching radius, and was reported before the 14:10 segment start; Orchard Road was recorded in speed band 1 (0–9 km/h) covering 14:00–14:10 [F14][F17]. That satisfies the RD-4(a) reasonable-cause exemption for the replaced stretch, so no amount is refundable for F4 [RD-4].

Segment 2 (F5) is not exempt. RD-5 exempts only the route the driver actually named before leaving the optimal route. The driver's 14:01 message named only "go round by Cavenagh" [F10], and the rider's 14:02 "Sure" plus a stop request [F11] answers that proposal [F12]; nothing in the chat names Beach Road or the far southward excursion that the track shows, reaching up to 1553 m off the optimal route [F5]. A mere "stop at a 7-Eleven on the way" is not consent to an unnamed, materially different corridor, and RD-3(b) is about rider-requested stops, not driver-proposed routes, so it cannot expand the consent either; the driver's own statement that he stopped "at the 7-Eleven I know on Beach Road" [F13] confirms the far location was the driver's choice [RD-5][RD-3]. Nor does RD-4 rescue it: the only traffic records touching this leg are speed bands, and a band alone does not exempt [F15][F16], while the accident record [F17] was matched to the earlier stretch in the trace [RD-4]. Segment 2 is therefore an unexempt detour of 2.83 km [F5][RD-1].

The refund follows RD-2's metered formula: the per-km rate is distance_fare ÷ distance_km = $13.14 ÷ 9.3 km = $1.4129/km [F9][F6], so 2.83 km × $1.4129/km = $4.00 (rounded to the cent) [F5][F9][RD-2]. The billed excess-distance line of $7.58 (5.4 km × $1.41/km) [F6] is the aggregate figure and is superseded by the segment-level computation.

The $1.08 waiting charge is not refunded [F7]. This is not a pickup-point waiting-fee case, so NS-6 does not apply, and the rider's request caused the stop [F11].

No account referral is issued. RD-6 requires route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1 for a repeated-breach flag, and the driver's 90-day profile shows 1 upheld dispute but route upheld = 0 (it is a no-show case) [F20], so the condition is not met [RD-6]. Rider-side profile facts [F19] are irrelevant to liability and are not used as the basis of any finding.
